t:
(a) Subsection (b) of section 108 of title 23, United States Code, is amended by striking out “this section” and inserting in lieu thereof “subsection (a) of this section”. 
    (b) 
Section 108 of title 23, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end thereof the following new subsection:

“(c) (1) There is hereby established in the Treasury of the United States a revolving fund to be known as the right-of-way revolving fund which shall be administered by the Secretary in carrying out the provisions of this subsection. Sums authorized to be appropriated to the right-of-way revolving fund shall be available for expenditure without regard to the fiscal year for which such sums are authorized.

“(2) 
For the purpose of acquiring rights-of-way for future construction of highways on any Federal-aid system and for making payments for the moving or relocation of persons, businesses, farms, and other existing uses of real property caused by the acquisition of such rights-of-way, in addition to the authority contained in subsection (a) of this section, the Secretary, upon request of a State highway department, is authorized to advance funds, without interest, to the State from amounts available in the right-of-way revolving fund, in accordance with rules and regulations prescribed by the Secretary. Funds so advanced may be used to pay the entire costs of projects for the acquisition of rights-of-way, including the net cost to the State of property management, if any, and related moving and relocation payments made pursuant to section 133 or chapter 5 of this title.


“(3) 
Actual construction of a highway on rights-of-way, with respect to which funds are advanced under this subsection, shall be commenced within a period of not less than two years nor more than seven years following the end of the fiscal year in which the Secretary approves such advance of funds, unless the Secretary, in his discretion, shall provide for an earlier termination date. Immediately upon the termination of the period of time within which actual construction must be commenced, in the case of any project where such construction is not commenced before such termination, or upon approval by the Secretary of the plans, specifications, and estimates for such project for the actual construction of a highway on rights-of-way with respect to which funds are advanced under this subsection, whichever shall occur first, the right-of-way revolving fund shall be credited with an amount equal to the Federal share of the funds advanced, as provided in section 120 of this title, out of any Federal-aid highway funds apportioned to the State in which such project is located and available for obligation for projects on the Federal-aid system of which such project is to be a part, and the State shall reimburse the Secretary in an amount equal to the non-Federal share of the funds advanced for deposit in, and credit to, the right-of-way revolving fund.” 
    (c) 
There is authorized to be appropriated, out of the highway trust fund, to the right-of-way revolving fund established by subsection (c) of section 108 of title 23, United States (lode, $100,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1970, $100,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1971, and $100,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1972.
 
    (d) 
On or before January 1 next preceding the commencement of each fiscal year for which funds are authorized to be appropriated to the right-of-way revolving fund by subsection (c) of this section, the Secretary shall apportion the funds so authorized for such fiscal year to the States. Each State shall be apportioned for such fiscal year an amount which bears the same percentage relationship to the total amount being apportioned under this subsection as I he total of nil apportionments made to such State for such fiscal year under paragraphs (1), (2), (3), and (5), of subsection (b) of section 104 of title 23, United States Code, bears to the total of all amounts apportioned under such paragraphs to all States for such fiscal year. Amounts apportioned under this subsection shall not be construed to be authorizations of appropriations for the construction, reconstruction, or improvement of the Interstate System for the purposes of subsection (g) of section 209 of the Highway Revenue Act of 1956. 
 
    (e) 
Funds apportioned to a State under this subsection (d) of this section shall remain available for obligation for advances to such State until October 1 of the fiscal year for which such apportionment is made. All amounts not advanced or obligated for advancement before such date shall revert to the right-of-way revolving fund and together with all other amounts credited and reimbursed to such fund shall be available for advances to the States to carry out subsection (c) of section 108 of title 23, United States Code, in an equitable manner, taking into consideration each State’s need for, and ability to use, such advances, in accordance with such rules and regulations as the Secretary of Transportation shall establish.

fable.w: The section directs the Secretary to prescribe rules and regulations governing advances from the right-of-way revolving fund, and the definition treats a grant of rulemaking authority as participation (as in the worked example on regulations). The tempting reading is that this is only a funding mechanism in which a State highway department requests advances, which would be a non-qualifying application for funds. That reading does not account for the two rulemaking clauses, which carry the Yes label on their own.
fable.s: in accordance with such rules and regulations as the Secretary of Transportation shall establish

opus.w: The section directs the Secretary to set rules and regulations for handing out revolving-fund advances to States. Under the definition and Example 6, requiring rulemaking counts as participation, because rulemaking brings in public comment. It is tempting to say 'No' because the State 'request' for advances is just an application for funds, which does not count. But the rulemaking language on its own settles the answer as 'Yes'.
opus.s: in accordance with such rules and regulations as the Secretary of Transportation shall establish
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** States "request" advances from the revolving fund. That is an application for funds, which does not count as participation under the definition. On that basis the answer might look like "No."
2. **Why that reading fails:** The section also gives the Secretary rulemaking authority. Advances are made "in accordance with rules and regulations prescribed by the Secretary." Leftover funds are also handed out under "such rules and regulations as the Secretary of Transportation shall establish." Under the definition and Example 6, requiring or authorizing rulemaking counts as participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes a revolving fund and outlines the process for states to request and receive advances. The 'request' from a state is a procedural trigger for a financial transaction, not a form of participation in a federal decision-making process. The Secretary's discretion is exercised through internal rules and regulations, without any requirement to consult with states, tribes, or the public before making decisions. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary, upon request of a State highway department, is authorized to advance funds, without interest, to the State from amounts available in the right-of-way revolving fund, in accordance with rules and regulations prescribed by the Secretary.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Secretary's discretion to determine "equitable manner" or "need" implies a process of consultation with states. However, the text explicitly states these decisions are made "in accordance with such rules and regulations as the Secretary of Transportation shall establish," which is an internal administrative process, not a requirement for external participation. Furthermore, the "request" from a State highway department is a trigger for a financial transaction (advancing funds), not a participatory decision-making process regarding policy or regulation. The section describes funding mechanisms, apportionment formulas, and administrative rules, none of which involve consulting with outside parties before a federal decision is made.
